rationale: C17 is the closest because it discusses combating Communist propaganda and confidence in Americans' support for freedom, but it neither addresses classroom instruction nor shares a distinctive verbal or structural pattern with the child. C07 connects free education with self-government, and C19 emphasizes education, facts, and public understanding, but those similarities are thematic rather than evidence of reused drafting. None supplies concrete language, an operative sequence, or administrative machinery materially reflected in the later telegram.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The competition for men's minds begins when they are students... discriminate between the American form of Government and the Soviet form.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The captive European peoples behind the Iron Curtain... are constantly bombarded by Communist propaganda... Radio Free Europe... fortifying their devotion to liberty.
shared_material.explanation: C17 shares an anti-Communist freedom-versus-Soviet theme, but not distinctive language or the child's education-focused drafting structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: our teachers are presented with a matchless opportunity to teach the truth freely
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a system of self-government and a system of education free of political restraints
shared_material.explanation: C07 links education and political freedom, but the resemblance is conceptual and too general to establish template reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When they have all the facts, I am confident they will make the correct choice
shared_material.parent_excerpt: With this opportunity to know the facts and understand the problems, I am convinced that the people of the United States will develop programs of effective action.
shared_material.explanation: C19 contains a loose facts-to-informed-action formulation in an educational context, but it is generic rhetoric rather than concrete shared drafting.
